prompt: How many degrees are in a full turn?

feedback.b: 180° is half a turn: a straight line.
feedback.c: Angles are not measured in hundreds like centimetres. A full turn is 360°.
feedback.d: 90° is a quarter turn: a right angle.

hints: A quarter turn is 90°. How many quarter turns make a full turn?
solution: A full turn is 4 quarter turns: $4 \times 90 = 360$°.

prompt: Match each type of angle to its size.
hints: A right angle is a square corner. A straight angle is a straight line.
solution: Acute: less than 90°. Right: exactly 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°. Straight: exactly 180°. Reflex: between 180° and 360°.

prompt: Which tool do we use to measure an angle?

feedback.b: A ruler measures length. It can't measure the amount of turn.
feedback.c: A thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius. Angles are measured in degrees too, but with a different tool.

hints: It is shaped like half a circle, with numbers from 0 to 180.
solution: A **protractor** measures angles in degrees.

prompt: What is the name for an angle that is more than 180° but less than 360°?
hints: It goes the long way round, more than a straight line.
solution: An angle between 180° and 360° is a **reflex** angle.

prompt: A clock shows exactly 3 o'clock. What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand?
hints: The minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand points to 3.
From 12 to 3 is a quarter of the way round the clock.
solution: From 12 to 3 is a quarter turn. A full turn is 360°, so a quarter turn is $360 \div 4 = 90$°. The angle is a right angle, **90°**.

prompt: Losa measures an angle with a protractor and says it is 130°. But the angle is clearly smaller than a right angle. What mistake has she most likely made?

options.text: She read the wrong scale. The angle is 50°.
She didn't make a mistake. The angle is 130°.
She should have added 90°. The angle is 220°.
She should have halved it. The angle is 65°.

feedback.b: 130° is obtuse, bigger than a right angle. That can't be right for an angle smaller than a square corner.
feedback.c: Adding 90° would make it even bigger. The angle is acute.
feedback.d: Halving isn't part of reading a protractor.

hints: A protractor has two scales. What do the two numbers at each mark add up to?
solution: The two scales on a protractor add to 180° at each mark. Losa read the wrong one: the real angle is $180 - 130 =$ **50°**, which is acute.

prompt: What does $\angle PQR$ mean?

options.text: The angle at Q, between the arms going to P and R
The angle at P, between the arms going to Q and R
The angle at R, between the arms going to P and Q
The length of the line from P to R

feedback.b: The first letter is not the vertex. That would be written $\angle QPR$.
feedback.c: The last letter is not the vertex. That would be written $\angle PRQ$.
feedback.d: The ∠ sign means an angle, not a length.

hints: The middle letter tells you where the vertex is.
solution: In angle notation the **middle letter is the vertex**. $\angle PQR$ is the angle at Q, between QP and QR.

prompt: A ladder leans against a wall. It makes an angle of 70° with the flat ground on one side. What is the angle between the ladder and the ground on the **other** side?
hints: The ground is a straight line.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
solution:
The two angles are on a straight line (the ground), so they add to 180°.

$180 - 70 = 110$, so the other angle is **110°**.

prompt: Put these angles in order from **smallest** to **largest**.
hints: A right angle is 90° and a straight angle is 180°.
solution: 45°, a right angle (90°), 120°, a straight angle (180°), 200°.

prompt: Select **all** the statements that are true.

options.text: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.
Angles at a point add up to 360°.
Vertically opposite angles add up to 180°.
A reflex angle is less than 180°.

hints: Think about a straight line (half a turn) and a full turn.
solution: True: angles on a straight line add to 180°, angles at a point add to 360°, and vertically opposite angles are equal. False: vertically opposite angles are equal (they don't have to add to 180°), and a reflex angle is **more** than 180°.

prompt: Two angles are on a straight line. One is 65°. Mere says the other angle is 295°, because $360 - 65 = 295$. What should the answer be?

options.text: 115°, because angles on a straight line add to 180°

feedback.b: 360° is for angles all the way round a point. A straight line is only half a turn.
feedback.c: Angles next to each other on a straight line are only equal if they are both 90°.
feedback.d: Angles that add to 90° make a right angle, not a straight line.

hints: How many degrees are on a straight line?
solution: Mere used 360°, which is for a full turn. On a straight line the angles add to 180°: $180 - 65 =$ **115°**.

prompt: A round pizza is cut from the centre into 8 equal slices. What is the angle at the centre of each slice?
hints: All the angles at the centre go the whole way round.
Angles at a point add to 360°. Share that equally between 8 slices.
solution:
The angles at the centre make a full turn of 360°.

$360 \div 8 = 45$, so each slice has an angle of **45°**.

prompt: Hana is facing north. She turns clockwise until she is facing south. How many degrees has she turned?
hints: North to east is a quarter turn clockwise.
How many quarter turns from north to south?
solution:
North → east is 90°, and east → south is another 90°.

$90 + 90 = 180$, so Hana turned **180°** (half a turn).

prompt: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles is 40°. Explain why the angle **vertically opposite** it must also be 40°. Use angles on a straight line in your answer.
modelAnswer: The angle next to the 40° angle is on a straight line with it, so it is 180 − 40 = 140°. The angle opposite the 40° angle is also next to that 140° angle on the other straight line, so it is 180 − 140 = 40°. So the vertically opposite angles are both 40°.

rubric.criterion: Uses angles on a straight line to find the angle next to 40° (140°)
Uses the other straight line to show the opposite angle is 180 − 140 = 40°

hints: First find the angle next to the 40° angle.
The opposite angle is next to that angle too, on the other line.
solution: The neighbouring angle is $180 - 40 = 140$°. The opposite angle sits on the other straight line with that 140° angle, so it is $180 - 140 = 40$°.

prompt: Which is bigger: the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 4 o'clock, or at 8 o'clock?

feedback.b: 8 is a bigger number, but the hour hand is 4 hours away from 12 going the other way.
feedback.c: At 4 o'clock the hour hand is 4 hours from 12. At 8 o'clock it is also 4 hours from 12, going the other way.
feedback.d: You can work it out: each hour on a clock is $360 \div 12 = 30$°.

hints: Each hour on a clock face is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°.
At 8 o'clock, how many hours is the hour hand from 12 the short way round?
solution: Each hour is $360 \div 12 = 30$°. At 4 o'clock the hands are 4 hours apart: $4 \times 30 = 120$°. At 8 o'clock they are also 4 hours apart the short way (from 8 up to 12): 120°. **They are the same size.**

prompt: Two straight lines cross, making four angles. One of the angles is 58°. What is the **total** of the other three angles?
hints: All four angles are around one point.
Angles at a point add up to 360°.
solution:
The four angles are at a point, so they add to 360°.

$360 - 58 = 302$°.

(Check: the other three are 122°, 58° and 122°, and $122 + 58 + 122 = 302$.)

prompt: Sione is facing west. He turns clockwise through 270°. Which way is he facing now?

feedback.b: That is a 90° turn clockwise from west. Sione turns three times as far.
feedback.c: That is a 180° turn (half a turn) from west.
feedback.d: He would face west again only after a full turn of 360°.

hints: 270° is three quarter turns.
Clockwise from west, the next direction is north.
solution: 270° is 3 quarter turns. Clockwise from west: north (90°), east (180°), south (270°). Sione faces **south**.

prompt: Explain how you can use a protractor to measure a **reflex** angle, even though a protractor only goes up to 180°.
modelAnswer: Measure the smaller angle between the two arms with the protractor. The smaller angle and the reflex angle go all the way round, so together they make 360°. Take the smaller angle away from 360°. For example, if the smaller angle is 70°, the reflex angle is 360 − 70 = 290°.

rubric.criterion: Says to measure the smaller angle between the arms
Explains taking it away from 360° because the two angles make a full turn (example optional)

hints: The reflex angle and the smaller angle together make a full turn.
solution: Measure the smaller angle, then subtract it from 360°, because the two angles together make a full turn.

prompt: A clock shows exactly 2 o'clock. What is the size of the **reflex** angle between the hour hand and the minute hand?
hints: Each hour on a clock face is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°.
Find the smaller angle first, then take it away from 360°.
solution:
Each hour is $360 \div 12 = 30$°. At 2 o'clock the hands are 2 hours apart: $2 \times 30 = 60$°.

The reflex angle is $360 - 60 =$ **300°**.

prompt: There are four angles around a point. One is a right angle, one is 80°, and the other two are equal. What is the size of each of the two equal angles?
hints: Angles at a point add to 360°. A right angle is 90°.
Take away the angles you know, then share what is left between the two equal angles.
solution:
Angles at a point add to 360°.

Known angles: $90 + 80 = 170$°.

The two equal angles together: $360 - 170 = 190$°.

Each one: $190 \div 2 =$ **95°**.

prompt: Kai cuts a round cake from the centre. The first piece has an angle of 60°, the second 75° and the third 90°. He cuts the rest of the cake into 3 equal pieces. What is the angle at the centre of each of those pieces?
hints: All the angles at the centre add up to 360°.
Find how much of the 360° is left, then share it between 3 pieces.
solution:
Angles at the centre add to 360°.

First three pieces: $60 + 75 + 90 = 225$°.

Left over: $360 - 225 = 135$°.

Each of the 3 equal pieces: $135 \div 3 =$ **45°**.
